title: Making a Christmas Door Wreath
description: Explore a festive ring of greenery through its supporting frame, tied bow, and small decorations.
cardDescription: Explore a festive ring of greenery through its supporting frame, tied bow, and small decorations.
focus: A wreath is a ring-shaped arrangement rather than a long hanging garland. The clues distinguish the structure underneath from the plant material and ornaments covering it.
solvingTip: Start with a shape or fastening, then identify the greenery or decoration.
words: Ring-shaped decoration hung on a door during many holidays
Long decorative strand of greenery rather than a closed ring
Evergreen plant associated with prickly leaves and winter berries
Climbing evergreen vine used in some holiday greenery
Underlying support holding a wreath's ring shape
Looped ribbon decoration tied onto a holiday ring
Narrow decorative fabric strip used for tying a bow
Thin metal strand securing greenery to a support
Closed circular shape of a traditional door wreath
Evergreen tree supplying needles and cones for decorations
Woody pine structure added to a winter arrangement
Small ringing ornament attached to a festive wreath
Small colorful fruit used as a greenery accent
Entrance panel on which the finished wreath hangs

answerNotes.WREATH: Wreaths appear in several traditions and seasons; this scene focuses on a Christmas arrangement.
answerNotes.GARLAND: Garland describes an extended strand, though it can also be looped into a design.
answerNotes.HOLLY: Many hollies have prickly leaves, but leaf form and berry color vary across species and varieties.
answerNotes.IVY: Ivy is a vine, unlike the woody branch material supplied by a pine tree.
answerNotes.FRAME: A frame provides structure, while greenery and ornaments cover or decorate it.

cardDescription: Look at a traditional painted nutcracker figure through its wooden body, moving jaw, and decorative costume.
subtheme: A Christmas Nutcracker on the Shelf
focus: Nutcrackers can be working tools or decorative figures. The clues distinguish a lever mechanism from the soldier-style details associated with many Christmas ornaments.
solvingTip: Separate a mechanical part from a painted costume feature.

answerNotes.NUTCRACKER: Some ornamental figures are primarily decorative and are not designed for practical shell cracking.
answerNotes.LEVER: A lever trades movement distance against force according to its geometry; it does not create energy.
answerNotes.JAW: The jaw is part of the mechanism rather than the hat or painted uniform.
answerNotes.HINGE: A hinge permits rotation between connected pieces.
answerNotes.SOLDIER: Soldier is one familiar decorative form rather than the only possible nutcracker design.

title: Opening an Advent Calendar
description: Explore a familiar holiday countdown through numbered flaps, small compartments, and the daily picture or surprise.
cardDescription: Explore a familiar holiday countdown through numbered flaps, small compartments, and the daily picture or surprise.
focus: Many commercial Advent calendars count the days from December 1 to Christmas. The Christian Advent season follows a liturgical calendar and does not always begin on that same date.
solvingTip: Use the clue’s category: calendar period, opening, material, or small compartment.
words: Christian season before Christmas named on a familiar countdown calendar

Decorative strip used to hang a fabric calendar

answerNotes.ADVENT: Liturgical Advent begins on a Sunday and varies in calendar date; many commercial calendars instead begin on December 1.
answerNotes.CALENDAR: A calendar can show an entire year or a selected countdown period.
answerNotes.FLAP: A flap is part of the paper construction, not the picture hidden beneath it.
answerNotes.POCKET: Pocket-style calendars use containers rather than necessarily having paper doors.
answerNotes.NUMBER: The number indicates order; the design and contents can vary widely.

title: A Snow Globe on the Mantel
description: Examine a decorative globe through its transparent dome, miniature scene, and drifting imitation snow.
cardDescription: Examine a decorative globe through its transparent dome, miniature scene, and drifting imitation snow.
subtheme: A Snow Globe on the Mantel
focus: A snow globe contains a small scene within a liquid-filled enclosure. The suspended pieces settle after movement, creating a snowfall effect without real frozen flakes.
solvingTip: Separate the enclosure, the contents, and the movement that sets them drifting.
words: Decorative liquid-filled ornament with drifting imitation snow, with spaces omitted

answerNotes.SNOWGLOBE: Snow globe is continuous in the grid; the white particles are decorative material rather than real snow.
answerNotes.DOME: A dome can be made from glass or another clear material; the shape does not require one specific substance.
answerNotes.FLAKE: The apparent flakes are small decorative particles, not ice crystals.
answerNotes.GLITTER: Glitter reflects light as it moves; it is different from a lamp that emits its own light.
answerNotes.SEAL: A seal closes the enclosure; it differs from the ornamental base supporting it.

title: Strings of Outdoor Holiday Lights
description: Recognize familiar decorative-lighting parts through bulbs, clips, cords, and a timer’s daily schedule.
cardDescription: Recognize familiar decorative-lighting parts through bulbs, clips, cords, and a timer’s daily schedule.
focus: The clues identify components and visual effects in a seasonal display. Modern LED strings and older lamp strings can differ in construction, so each definition names the specific part or effect.
solvingTip: Use the component’s purpose: making light, holding it, connecting it, or controlling the timing.
words: Connected length of decorative holiday lamps
Fitting receiving a replaceable lamp base
Light-emitting diode, expressed as three initials

answerNotes.STRING: A light string contains connected lamps; the exact wiring and lamp design vary by product.
answerNotes.SOCKET: A socket holds a compatible bulb; some integrated light designs do not have separately replaceable lamps.
answerNotes.LED: LED names a light-producing electronic component rather than a particular color or exterior shape.
answerNotes.TIMER: A timer controls when lights operate, distinct from a dimmer controlling brightness.
answerNotes.FUSE: A fuse is a protective component rather than an ordinary on-off switch.
